transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
You can add freedom and feathers to the long list of President Trump's pardons since he returned to office last year.
This afternoon, President Trump led the annual White House tradition of sparking a pair of turkeys,
sparing a pair of turkeys, that is, from becoming Thanksgiving dinner.
Trump got a picture with one turkey, apparently the other wandered off somewhere in the bushes.
Before the photo op, Trump shifted the focus from freedom and feathers to an economy that he proclaims to be strong on his watch,
his renovation projects, including the ballroom, what he describes as the success of his immigration policies,
and the U.S. war with Iran. Then Trump turned back to expressing gratitude to security forces ahead of Thanksgiving.
A top house Democrat is expanding his investigation into the venture capital fund 1789 Capital.
NPR's Barbara Sprunt reports the President's eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., was brought in as a partner in the firm days after his father won re-election last year
and returned to the White House to become the 47th President of the United States.
Jamie Raskin, the likely incoming chair of the House Judiciary Committee, sent letters on Monday evening to four companies backed by 1789 Capital,
defense contractor Hadrian, vape maker Jewell, prediction market Polymarket, and the online firearms seller Grabagun.
The Maryland Democrat requested two years' worth of documents.
He's investigating whether the President's son used his political influence to boost the companies.
An attorney representing 1789 Capital called the allegations "personal attacks untethered to actual evidence."
This is one part of a broader oversight agenda for Democrats when they take control of Congress in January.
Barbara Sprunt, NPR News, Washington.
The rate of newborns receiving vaccination against hepatitis B has fallen sharply from 80 percent in 2022 to just under 66 percent this year.
According to new findings in the New England Journal of Medicine, here's NPR's Maria Godoy.
Last winter, a federal advisory panel to the CDC voted to end a long-standing recommendation that all newborns get the hepatitis B vaccine.
The new study offers the first glimpse of how vaccination rates have changed since then.
Study co-author Nina Masters of healthcare data analytics firm Triveda says while vaccination rates had been sliding for several years before the panels vote,
"There's been a lot of national-level miscommunication and confusing information, changing recommendations,
and it's certainly not helping parents to feel clear on what they should do."
Hepatitis B infections in infants are highly likely to lead to chronic infection and serious complications like liver cancer later in life.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
This is NPR.
The prime minister of Singapore says the country does not want to become a backdoor for advanced U.S. semiconductor chips flowing to China.
This, as the U.S. blacklist the Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed.
Former Megaspeed executive Alice Wong was suspected of being a Chinese spy.
At the same time, she was having an affair with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Wong.
Yan Kamens and Ruby reports.
Singapore's prime minister Lawrence Wong says the country will work with American authorities to develop a mechanism that allows the U.S. to enforce its own export controls,
adding that the island nation does not want to be "used and abused as a conduit by companies to circumvent America's export controls."
The statement comes as the U.S. placed Singapore-based Megaspeed on a trade blacklist.
That's Yan Kamens and Ruby reporting.
Thanksgiving travel is pricier this year, especially airfares. Here's NPR's Willa Rubin.
The big reason prices are up? Jet fuel.
It's up nearly 90 percent this year, according to the travel tech company Hopper.
Jet fuel comes from crude oil, and there's been less of that coming out of the Middle East this year due to the war in Iran.
It's meant less jet fuel to go around, so even higher demand.
The price for a barrel of crude has dropped in recent weeks, but for travelers, most people book their tickets a few months in advance.
When it comes to the price of that jet fuel, air carriers are absorbing some of those costs, but they're also passing them on.
Tickets for Thanksgiving are up about 30 percent compared to last year, according to Hopper.
AAA said in its Thanksgiving travel forecast, the average round-trip domestic ticket price cost $800.
This week on NPR's Up First, NVIDIA's CEO is back on the job.
What does that mean for your wallet?
The Thanksgiving travel rush begins in the aftermath of airline and FAA meltdowns.
What does that mean for your plans?
Also, the holiday shopping season is underway.
It's a lot to track during the busy time of the year, so make our short, daily episodes part of your morning routine.
Listen every weekday to Up First from NPR News.

topics.text: Trump pardons a turkey at White House annual Thanksgiving tradition, touting economy and immigration
House Judiciary Democrat Jamie Raskin expands probe into 1789 Capital and Donald Trump Jr. ties
Hepatitis B vaccination rate for newborns drops from 80 percent in 2022 to under 66 percent
Singapore's prime minister vows to stop being conduit for US chip export evasion after Megaspeed blacklisting
Thanksgiving airfares up about 30 percent this year as jet fuel prices surge amid Iran war
